items.title: Support reassignment of a completed worker with an explicit worker role
items.context: After one subagent/worker assignment completes, the operator needs a way to assign follow-up work under the worker role. The path may use a fresh context and explicit instructions instead of full-history inheritance.
items.userSees: User sees `Worker reassignment ready`, `mode: fresh-context`, `role: lattice-implementer`, the old dispatch id, the new dispatch id, and a promptFile path for the follow-up worker.

happy.desc: Given an accepted/completed dispatch, `dispatch_reassign` with `role=lattice-implementer` and explicit instructions creates a new follow-up dispatch whose output names the previous dispatch, new dispatch, fresh-context mode, requested role, and promptFile.

edge.desc: If no role is supplied, the follow-up still starts as the default worker role rather than depending on full-history fork role inference.

adversarial.desc: The original dispatch record is not overwritten or rerun; the new dispatch receives its own id and stores parentDispatchId pointing to the previous dispatch.

verificationEvidence.note: Dispatch smoke now uses and asserts the canonical explicit worker role lattice-implementer in dispatch_reassign output, pack metadata, and generated prompt, covering the user-visible role named by the intent.
Dispatch smoke asserts omitted-role reassignment returns explicit default role overflow-worker and renders Role: overflow-worker in the generated prompt.
Dispatch smoke snapshots the original dispatch record before reassignment, verifies it is unchanged afterward, and verifies the new record parentDispatchId points to the previous dispatch.

items.title: Preserve useful prior worker context without depending on full-history fork
items.context: The follow-up launch material should include bounded prior result or operator-provided context, but must not require inheriting the entire parent conversation. It should be clear when continuity is summary-based rather than full memory-based.
items.userSees: User opens the generated prompt and sees `Continuity: summary-only fresh context`, the previous dispatch id, explicit follow-up instructions, and no claim that full conversation history was inherited.

happy.desc: The generated follow-up prompt includes the requested role, objective, explicit execution instructions, and a summary-only continuity block referencing the previous dispatch.

edge.desc: When the previous dispatch has a receipt or transcript summary missing, the follow-up prompt still renders bounded lineage without pretending to have full memory.

adversarial.desc: Reassignment output and prompt do not contain wording that claims full-history inheritance, receipt verification, release readiness, or production DONE.

verificationEvidence.note: Dispatch smoke reads reassignment prompts and asserts they include Role, Objective, Fresh-context Continuity, mode fresh-context, previous dispatch id, and summary-only continuity wording.

Dispatch smoke now treats an unrun prepared previous dispatch with no accepted-local receipt as a blocked/rejected edge case: dispatch_reassign throws a clear completed/accepted requirement error, emits no Worker reassignment ready text, and creates no follow-up dispatch. Accepted reassignment still renders summary-only fresh-context continuity.

Dispatch smoke asserts reassignment prompts include no full-history fork is required and do not match forbidden claims for full-history inheritance, receipt verification, production DONE, or authority changes.

items.title: Verify role-aware worker reassignment behavior
items.context: Add focused coverage showing that a completed worker can receive a second assignment with a requested worker role and explicit instructions, and that the generated launch guidance does not depend on full-history fork behavior.
items.userSees: User sees the verification run pass with assertions covering `dispatch_reassign`, requested role propagation, fresh-context prompt wording, parentDispatchId lineage, and unchanged dispatch_resume behavior.

happy.desc: Smoke coverage proves a completed fake worker can be reassigned with an explicit worker role and follow-up instructions, producing the expected output and prompt metadata.

edge.desc: Regression coverage proves existing dispatch_resume still resumes/reruns the original dispatch metadata and does not silently create a follow-up reassignment.

adversarial.desc: Process-fact verification recognizes dispatch_reassign as an L1 diagnostic-only dispatch command with no gate evidence, receipt verification, or production DONE semantics.

verificationEvidence.note: Post-code-commit BUG-001 regression: dispatch_reassign with role lattice-implementer rewrites inherited Work in role execution instructions to Work in role: lattice-implementer. and the generated prompt does not retain Work in role: overflow-worker.
Dispatch smoke adds a dispatch_resume regression proving resume returns the original dispatch id and does not create a follow-up reassignment record.
Process fact contract verification still passes with dispatch_reassign registered as L1 lattice-dispatch metadata after adding the previous-dispatch accepted-local eligibility guard.
TypeScript build passed after adding dispatch_reassign core, handler, catalog, policy, config, process-fact, and smoke coverage.
Unattended dispatch smoke passed after command registration and dispatch policy changes.
